holisticNarrative.summary:
The TechCare export documentation is more concrete than many b(10) pages because it discloses a recognizable data dictionary with typed columns and nullability across 12 CSV domains. The assumptions section is also unusually explicit in describing INMATES.ID as the demographic key linking other tables, which materially helps migration planning.

At the same time, the architecture is intentionally hybrid: CSV for many operational tables, C-CDA for several clinically important categories, and PDF for images/scanned records. That design is practical for interoperability but introduces reconstruction risk because non-CSV portions are described only at section-title level without sample payloads or machine-readable schema.

Under designated-record-set EHI scope, the major unresolved question is not audit/system data, but whether patient financial records (insurance/claims/payments) and other decision-relevant domains are actually present in outputs despite not being explicitly documented. The result is a usable but partial posture: implementable with effort, but still dependent on assumptions and follow-up validation using real export files.
standoutObservations: The dictionary is image-based but still includes strong field/type/nullability detail for CSV tables.
INMATES.ID relationship language is explicit and useful for join strategy planning.
C-CDA and PDF sections are semantically broad but structurally thin in the absence of sample payloads.
No explicit insurance/claims/payments export categories are documented despite potential product-level relevance.

notableFacts: The export documentation explicitly supports both single-patient and all-patients workflows and states single-patient export can run without developer assistance.
TechCare declares a three-format export strategy: CSV, C-CDA, and PDF.
The data dictionary documents 12 named CSV table categories with field names, SQL-like data types, descriptions, and nullability.
The assumptions section declares INMATES.ID as the demographic table primary key and foundational link across other tables.
C-CDA-only listed domains include Medication Administrations, Vital Signs, Diagnostic Results, Treatment Plans, Social History, Assessments, Functional Status, and Mental Status.
Images and scanned paper records are documented as PDF outputs for encounter-history continuity.
